title: Group rallies against data centres in North American Day of Protest
key_facts: A few dozen protesters gathered at Calgary City Hall on Saturday 3 Oct 2026 as part of a North American Day of Protest Against Data Centres.
Rallies were planned across North America, including at the Alberta legislature in Edmonton and in Lethbridge and Grande Prairie.
The Calgary event was hosted by Alberta Anti-AI; coordinator Jenna Abbas said environmental assessments are thin and information is kept from the public.
Protesters' concerns centered on water and energy use, natural gas consumption, farmland, tax breaks and a proposed data center near a wetland in Chestermere.

Alberta's technology minister Nate Glubish said projects must earn approvals from independent bodies and undergo environmental reviews, and the province is developing siting standards to keep large data centers away from residential areas.
quote_evidence: A small group of protesters gathered outside City Hall Saturday morning for a demonstration as part of the North American Day of Protest Against Data Centres.

"There's such a rush to build these data centers, very little environmental assessments going on, and a lot of information is being hidden from the public," said Jenna Abbas, coordinator with Alberta Anti-AI.
Projects must earn approvals from independent bodies and undergo environmental assessments and reviews before they can proceed, he said.
why_it_matters_hint: Organized local opposition to data centers is now coordinated across North America, with water use and secrecy the main complaints.
notes: Small turnout in Calgary; article covers one city of a continent-wide protest day.
